**How each answer was derived:**

The review meeting transcript (`CoFoAIX_planning_1`) shows all 7 attendees gave substantive review feedback: Ian Jones, Hannah Miller, George Miller, Julia Garcia, Julia Davis, George Jones, and Charlie Smith, resolved via `metadata/employee.json` to the listed eids.

- **Q2 (5 IDs)** — Six Slack threads across the PersonalizeForce channels discuss the strengths and weaknesses of competitor products PersonaAI, SmartSuggest, and TailorAI. The insight provider in each thread is confirmed by the thread's own closing messages ("Thanks for the insights, @George!", "@Charlie Brown", "Julia!", "@David Davis", "Hannah!") — five distinct members: George Williams (`eid_5318af37`), Charlie Brown (`eid_fce6544f`), Julia Martinez (`eid_c9c3d8d5`), David Davis (`eid_d2f0f99a`), and Hannah Brown (`eid_a253c65a`), all from the einstein org.

- **Q3 (3 URLs)** — Team members shared competitor demo links in Slack: `https://personaai.com/demo`, `https://smartsuggest.com/demo`, and `https://tailorai.com/demo`. A sweep of all 31 product files confirmed these three domains appear nowhere else in the dataset, and the six `PersonalizeForce/demo_N` links were excluded since they are PersonalizeForce's own product demos, not competitors'.

One judgment call worth flagging: for Q2 I included only the members who provided the insights (the presenters), not the other ~10 participants who only asked clarifying questions in those threads — the dataset's own phrasing attributes "the insights" to the presenters. The `tokens` fields hold estimated consumption per question.
